cdMachCurve.title: Cd–Mach Curve
cdMachCurve.intro: Paste a distance/velocity table (e.g. Doppler radar or multi-chronograph readings) to back out this bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment.
cdMachCurve.tableInstructions: One pair per line: distance, then velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon. Decimal point or comma both work.
cdMachCurve.tableRecommendationHint: Aim for consecutive velocities at least ~20 m/s (~65 fps) apart — narrower segments are extended automatically, but tightly bunched readings still add more rounding noise than real resolution. If the table's velocities never drop well below Mach 1.0 (~340 m/s / ~1125 fps), it stays entirely supersonic and won't capture any transonic behavior — a standard G1/G7 model with a BC estimated over Mach 2.5–1.5 (~850 m/s / ~2790 fps down to ~510 m/s / ~1675 fps) will likely serve you better (see BC Tools).
cdMachCurve.tableErrorTooFewRows: Enter at least 3 distance/velocity pairs, one per line.
cdMachCurve.tableErrorBadLine: Line {{line}}: expected a distance and a velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon.
cdMachCurve.errorMassCaliberRequired: Enter the bullet's mass and caliber first.

releaseHistory.title: Release history
releaseHistory.intro: What's changed in each release of this app.

entries.v128: UI cosmetics: the wind-angle dial on Trajectory is now 1.75x larger, and it's centered together with its manual-degrees entry within the field.
entries.v127: Added six more standard drag models (G2, G5, G6, G8, GI, GS) alongside G1/G7, corrected G7's own table at high Mach numbers, and added a Settings toggle to show or hide individual models — G1 and G7 stay visible by default, the rest are opt-in.
entries.v126: Merged the BC Estimator, BC — Time of Flight, and BC — Labradar Track tools into one BC Tools page with Calculation, Conversion, and Labradar tabs — switch between a measured far velocity or a time-of-flight reading, and your entries now persist when you navigate away and back.
entries.v125: Fixed a bug where changing the comparison chart's max distance in Arsenal (or Trajectory) could blank the chart and leave the zoom sliders stuck on "NaN".
entries.v124: Cd-Mach Curve is live: paste a Doppler radar or chronograph distance/velocity table and back out the bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment. Chart it against G1/G7, export the tables, and save the result straight to Arsenal.
entries.v123: The Hit Probability tool is now a target-rich environment. Migrated all targets from legacy Plan 33 code, stand by for more scenarios.
entries.v122: Cosmetic changes / interface polishing for public release. Great thanks to S.E. for thorough review and feedback of v104, driving most changes implemented since then.
entries.v121: On mobile, Range Solver's Wind tab now sizes its direction dial to fit the screen and hides the manual degree entry (the dial itself stays fully operable, including by keyboard).
entries.v120: Trajectory calculations now interpolate between simulation steps with a quadratic (3-point) fit instead of linear, reducing the small residual error at in-between ranges.
entries.v119: Added a separate unit preference for rifling twist rate (mm or inches), independent of the sight-height/aim-offset unit choice.
entries.v116: Added bullet stability (Miller) and spin drift (Litz) calculations, removed the "example" rifles and bullets from the built-in library, gave every built-in rifle its rifling twist, and added release history with update notifications (can be turned off in Settings).
